title: Generalized $m$-body mean-field projections for classical simulation of $d$-dimensional Heisenberg-picture dynamics
authors: Federico Tomás B. Pérez, Gabriela Wójtowicz, Matthias Kost, Martin B. Plenio
abstract: Classical simulation of quantum many-body dynamics is challenged by the rapid growth of operator complexity, particularly in higher dimensions where tensor-network methods become increasingly demanding. We develop state-adapted Pauli-weight propagation based on generalized $m$-body mean-field projections, which compress many-body observables into optimal low-body representations in a covariance geometry induced by the initial state. Combined with adaptive Krylov-like restricted Heisenberg dynamics, this provides an alternative to conventional Hilbert--Schmidt Pauli-weight truncation. We derive necessary and conditional sufficient bounds on low-body approximation accuracy using standard operator complexity measures and characterize possible dynamical failure mechanisms of the state-adapted method. Numerical benchmarks demonstrate substantial state-dependent accuracy gains, while identifying regimes of reduced accuracy or violations of Pauli spectral bounds. For a three-dimensional system of $80$ interacting spins, our method achieves strong body-order convergence, close agreement with independently converging tensor-network simulations, and substantially smaller sparse Pauli representations. These results establish state-adapted Pauli propagation as a promising approach to classical simulation of higher-dimensional coherent many-body dynamics.
summary: This paper introduces a novel state-adapted Pauli propagation technique to tackle the exponential complexity barrier in simulating quantum many-body dynamics. By projecting observables onto low-body representations using a covariance geometry, it offers a computationally efficient alternative to conventional truncation methods. The results demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving high accuracy for simulating higher-dimensional spin systems.
main_problem: The rapid growth of operator complexity challenges the classical simulation of quantum many-body dynamics, especially in higher dimensions.
main_result: The proposed state-adapted Pauli propagation method achieves strong body-order convergence and shows substantial state-dependent accuracy gains compared to conventional truncation schemes.
method: The method uses generalized m-body mean-field projections within a covariance geometry to compress high-body observables into optimal low-body representations, combined with adaptive Krylov-like restricted Heisenberg dynamics.
model_or_system: The dynamics are studied for interacting spin systems governed by a Hamiltonian in the Heisenberg picture, applicable to d-dimensional lattices.
key_observables: Operator complexity, Pauli weight, body order, and the expectation value of the observable $O_S$.
important_parameters: The body order $m$ (the truncation level) and the dimensionality $d$ of the system.
main_assumptions: The method relies on projecting observables onto a low-body subspace defined by the covariance geometry induced by the initial state $\sigma_0$.
figures_summary: The notes mention comparisons of computational scaling (NNZ counts, wall times) between the covariance projection and standard Hilbert-Schmidt Pauli-weight truncation for various body orders.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the Heisenberg picture, introduces the state-adapted projection, details the restricted dynamics, derives error bounds, and concludes with numerical benchmarks.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, state-dependent alternative to standard tensor network or Pauli-weight truncation methods for simulating complex quantum dynamics, which is highly relevant for simulating interacting many-body systems.
